newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Aircraft Industries reschedules bank debt.
newsitem.headline: Israel Aircraft Industries reschedules bank debt.

text.p: State-owned Israel Aircraft Industries (IAI) said on Sunday it had signed a debt-rescheduling accord with a consortium of Israel banks.
"We hope that with the signing of this agreement, IAI will be able to return to a normal and orderly work routine," said chief executive Moshe Keret in a statement.

Under the accord, the banks agreed to reschedule IAI's debt over eight years following a two-year grace period. The banks agreed to increase IAI's credit line to $310 million from the current $210 million, while the Israeli government agreed to inject $122 million in equity investment into the company.
In addition, the sides agreed that an independent accounting firm would examine future large-scale projects undertaken by IAI, which manufactures and maintains aircraft and makes avionics equipment.
Nir Gilad, IAI's new vice president for finance, said he hoped the company would begin reducing a major portion of its debt owed to suppliers.
